span.term: PV neurons pool a wider range of excitatory inputs and receive stronger subthreshold drive, so more of that input crosses spike threshold, producing broad, weakly selective spike tuning

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Non-selective local connectivity from excitatory cells onto inhibitory (especially PV) cells pools inputs with many different preferred frequencies onto one interneuron

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SOM neurons bypass the direct ascending (feedforward) pathway and are instead driven through slower horizontal circuits, which is why their input is delayed
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV cells pool excitatory input from neurons with a wide range of preferred frequencies because excitatory-to-PV connectivity is unselective

span.label: PV cells also convert input to output more efficiently, so a broad input becomes an even broader spike tuning

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · trough-to-peak interval —operationalised-as→ PV
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named neither. This clause names both and states the identification criterion - PV cells are recognised BY their trough-to-peak interval. — strength of the relation: 0.8 — SCOPED: valid 'for cell-attached recording in layer 2/3'. The same criterion in extracellular unit recording is what the paper criticises
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV —contrasted-with→ SOM
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: broader tuning, lower threshold, stronger and earlier responses - four separable measures, all differing
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (`same-as` ASSERTED FROM EQUALITY ON ONE PROPERTY) · SOM —same-as→ excitatory neurons
span.note: RETRACTED: `same-as` ASSERTED FROM EQUALITY ON ONE PROPERTY. The span: 'PV neurons had TRFs twice as broad as those of SOM and excitatory neurons, while THE LATTER 2 DID NOT DIFFER IN THEIR TRF BANDWIDTHS.' SOM cells and excitatory neurons are not the same thing; they failed to differ on a SINGLE MEASURE, in a sentence whose subject is PV. `same-as` is the strongest claim in the vocabulary and it is here standing on one bandwidth comparison. A category claim is relative to the features tested (Somogyi2005/Raposo2014), and this one names its feature in its own span. — strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — same FREQUENCY SELECTIVITY only; they differ in threshold, timing and jitter. A partial identity, weighted low on purpose
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · PV —operationalised-as→ feedforward inhibition
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span described the timing of PV excitatory drive without naming feedforward inhibition. This sentence names both and states what PV neurons PROVIDE - 'broadly tuned, feedforward inhibition for a rapid control of ascending inputs'. — strength of the relation: 0.9 — the role is inferred from timing - PV cells are driven with excitatory cells and spike before them
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Parvalbumin (PV) inhibitory neurons in layer 2/3 auditory cortex have broader tonal receptive fields, lower intensity thresholds and stronger tone-evoked spiking than somatostatin (SOM) neurons.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SOM neurons are as sharply frequency-tuned as excitatory neurons even though they too receive a broad range of excitatory input.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both the synaptic input onset and the spike onset of SOM neurons occur significantly later than those of PV and excitatory neurons.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Measured 10 dB above threshold, PV receptive fields were twice as broad as those of SOM and excitatory neurons, which did not differ from each other.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SOM neurons required significantly louder tones to respond than PV or excitatory neurons, implying they cannot supply inhibition at low sound intensities.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SOM neurons fired with significantly less precise timing, showing larger first-spike jitter than PV and excitatory neurons.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV neurons converted almost their whole synaptic input range into spike output (highest spike-range/input-range ratio), whereas SOM neurons converted the least.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tone-evoked subthreshold depolarizations (EPSPs) were significantly larger in PV neurons than in SOM or excitatory neurons.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Every recorded PV cell had a spike trough-to-peak interval below 0.5 ms while every recorded excitatory cell was above 0.5 ms, so waveform width separates the two classes in layer 2/3.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV neurons fired spontaneously at a significantly higher rate than excitatory cells.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The three cell groups were recorded at statistically indistinguishable cortical depths, so the broad PV tuning is not a depth-sampling artefact.
